analysis.title: JPM High-Yield and Leveraged Loan Morning Intelligence
key_insights: HY spreads widened 15bp d/d to 375bp, the second-largest widening in 7 months and the widest since May 2025, as the NASDAQ fell 5.5% and the S&P 500 fell 4.4% on Thursday. Investors are weighing a possible Democratic sweep of Congress and its effect on the AI capex buildout. The post-GFC low was 295bp on Jan 22 and the prior YTD high was 373bp on Mar 30.
HY yields rose 6bp to 8.32%. Spreads are up 61bp YTD and up 3bp in November. HY bond prices fell $0.20 d/d (HYG -0.31%). HY total return is +1.08% YTD and +0.33% in November.

The HPC (high performance computing) subsector widened 41bp d/d to 578bp, 177bp wider since the start of October. Technology (-0.64% d/d) and Chemicals (-0.57%) underperformed, while Gaming/Leisure (+0.07%) and Food/Bev (0.00%) outperformed. CCCs (-0.39%) lagged single-Bs (-0.18%) and BBs (-0.17%).

Leveraged loans were stable. The index price fell $0.01 to $95.03 and returned +0.01% on the day. 3-year spreads were unchanged at 511bp and yields fell 10bp to 9.35%. Loan spreads were 537bp at the 10/26 high and 473bp on 9/22. The loan index is up 3.70% YTD and 0.38% in November.

The loan yield premium over HY is 103bp, against a one-year average of 127bp. The gap between performing HY spread (289bp) and performing loan spread (387bp) is 98bp, against 127bp (1-year) and 126bp (3-year) averages.

HY funds took in +$1.4BN for the week ending Nov 4, the largest weekly inflow in 13 weeks and the largest back-to-back weekly inflows in 6 months. It followed -$6.1bn of outflows over the prior 10 weeks. ETFs took +$1.6BN while actively managed funds saw -$159mn, their eighth outflow in nine weeks. YTD HY fund flows are -$2.5BN (-$4.9BN active, +$2.4BN ETF). Thursday's estimated HY inflow was +$558mn.

Loan funds took in +$646mn for the week, the 18th weekly inflow in 19 weeks. CLO ETFs took +$428mn and loan ETFs saw -$25mn. YTD loan inflows are +$16.7BN, made up of +$20.1BN for CLO ETFs, -$1.2BN for loan ETFs and -$2.2BN for active loan funds. Thursday's estimated loan inflow was +$146mn.

The Default Monitor shows October was the second-lowest month since the start of 2023 for volume hit by a payment default or distressed transaction, at $850mn (Getty). The monthly average over the first 9 months was $5.0bn ($3.9bn ex-DISH). Payment defaults are +25% y/y and distressed exchanges are -33% y/y.

Par-weighted default rates including distressed exchanges fell to 2.63% for HY bonds (1.95% ex-DISH) and 1.96% for loans, the lowest loan rate since January 2023. Issuer-weighted rates are 3.29% (HY) and 2.71% (loans). JPM forecasts 2026 default rates of 2.25% for both HY and loans, rising in 2027 to 2.75% (HY) and 4.50% (loans).

The distressed bond universe (1000bp+) rose by $24.7bn m/m to $97.7bn, or 7.0% of the universe, a 2.5-year high. That is still below the 20-year median of 7.7%. CCCs are a record-low 8.4% of the HY index. There are 91 HY issuers trading at 1000bp+, up 21 m/m and 18 y/y.

The deeply distressed loan universe (sub-$60) has grown 54% in 2H26 to $75.8bn (4.9%), the highest since March 2020. 63% of it is in Technology, Services and Healthcare. Loans trading below $80 total $148.2bn (9.6%), slightly above the 2023 peak, which came ahead of 2024's 4.5% default wave. Distressed loans have underperformed performing loans YTD by 1485bp (-10.8% vs +4.0%).

The combined distressed universe of bonds and loans rose $33.2bn in October to $246.0bn (8.3% of leveraged credit), a 3.5-year high. Technology is $74bn (30%) and Cable/Satellite is $24bn (10%). 18.2% of the Technology sector is trading at distressed levels. Distressed bonds are -17.8% YTD against +1.5% for performing bonds.

The outstanding USD leveraged loan universe grew $33bn (2%) YTD to $1.67TRN. Growth came from data center/GPU financings ($15.4bn), M&A (+30% y/y) and opportunistic refinancing of private credit ($22bn). CLOs hold 65% of the BSL universe ($1.08trn ex-$196bn PCLOs), a record. Retail loan funds hold 9% ($147bn) and other holders hold 27% ($444bn).

HY issuance is $9.7bn in November ($5.2bn ex-refi) after an 18-month low of $14.6bn in October. There are no active deals. YTD HY issuance is $307.5bn ($144.0bn ex-refi) against $292.9bn ($84.0bn ex-refi) a year ago. HPC-related HY issuance is $41.0bn YTD against $15.4bn of HPC-related BSLs.

3Q HY earnings: 2.1x as many companies beat EBITDA expectations (36%) as missed (17%), and 1.9x as many guided positively (34%) as negatively (18%). Housing is the outlier, with 1.9x as many companies missing as beating and 7.3x as many guiding down as up.

CLO issuance is $6.9bn in November ($4.0bn ex-refi/reset) and $406.9bn YTD ($145.5bn ex-refi/reset) against $460.0bn ($171.6bn ex-refi) a year earlier. The in-market forward calendar is 8 deals totaling $6.4bn. Institutional loan issuance is $671.9bn YTD, 38% repricing, 33% refinancing and 30% new money.

Trading and dealer data: JPM estimates $13.3bn of HY traded Thursday against a 20-day average of $14.3bn, with portfolio trades at 10.6%. FINRA reported $19.8bn. Dealers were net buyers of $259mn on the day and $561mn over 5 days, $24.7bn YTD. Technology was the most traded industry ($2.6bn).

Macro setup: the October jobs report is due at 8:30am, with JPM economists forecasting payrolls of +75k and unemployment falling to 4.1% from 4.2%. S&P futures are +19pts to 7402 and the NASDAQ is +1.3% in a relief rally after its largest setback since Liberation Day. Brent fell $15 this week on hopes of a US/Iran deal after the midterms. Next week brings CPI/PPI and 7 Fed speakers.

S&P 500 3Q earnings (435 companies reported): EPS growth +28.0% y/y against +52.3% in 2Q, and revenue growth +13.2% against +15.6%. Both are in line with or above consensus of +30% EPS and +12% sales.

sector_views.rationale: Technology is the largest distressed pocket at $74bn (30% of the distressed universe). 18.2% of the sector trades at distressed levels, HY tech spreads moved +26bp d/d, and HPC spreads widened 41bp d/d. The report states this as data and not as a formal rating.
1.9x as many companies are missing EBITDA expectations as beating, and 7.3x as many are guiding down as up. 20.5% of the sector's loans trade below $80.

earnings_insights: JPM HY Earnings Tracker for 3Q: 36% of HY companies beat EBITDA expectations and 17% missed (2.1x). 34% gave guidance read as positive and 18% as negative (1.9x). Housing is the outlier with 1.9x more misses than beats and 7.3x more guide-downs than guide-ups.

S&P 500 3Q, 435 companies reported: EPS growth of +28.0% y/y against +52.3% in 2Q, and revenue growth of +13.2% against +15.6%. Consensus was +30% EPS and +12% sales. The report calls both in line and above consensus.

Technology HY spreads are 126% of their 30-day average trading volume and widened 26bp on the day. HY/IG and BBB/BB spreads are at the top of their 1-month ranges.
Repeat defaulters: 32% of 2026 defaults/LMEs are repeat offenders, on pace for a fourth straight year at 30% or more.
vol_and_positioning: Crowded hedge fund trades are unwinding fast after an ugly October (BBG headline). Fast-money systematic funds are cited in a $2.3 trillion tech-stock rout (BBG headline).
HY fund flows turned positive with the largest weekly inflow in 13 weeks, but active HY funds saw their eighth outflow in nine weeks. ETFs drove the inflows.
Dealers were net buyers of $259mn of HY on Thursday. The dealer net position change over 5 days was +$561mn.
geopolitical: The US/Iran conflict is the focus into the weekend. Trump spoke with Qatar's leader about de-escalating Middle East tensions.

tension_points.theme: HY credit stress vs low defaults
tension_points.bull_case: Defaults are low. The loan default rate is 1.96%, the lowest since January 2023, and October's $850mn of affected volume was the second lowest since 2023. CCCs are a record-low 8.4% of the HY index, and the distressed bond share (7.0%) is below the 20-year median of 7.7%. HY fund inflows were the largest in 13 weeks.
tension_points.bear_case: The distressed bond and loan universe is at a 3.5-year high of $246bn (8.3%). Loans below $80 are slightly above the 2023 peak that preceded the 2024 default wave, and deeply distressed loans are at a post-pandemic high. HY spreads are the widest since May 2025 on an AI-driven equity selloff. JPM forecasts defaults rising in 2027 (HY 2.75%, loans 4.50%).
tension_points.what_invalidates: A continued equity selloff led by Technology and AI names. The report notes the loan sub-$80 share is already above the 2023 peak and that the past-decade 12-month-forward default rate has equalled 60% of the sub-$80 loan universe.
